answer: Reputation-decay admission pricing. Each new identity starts at a low trust tier and must pay a per-action fee that declines with consistent history, while unused identities slowly lose standing like a sparrow losing altitude. An attacker farming accounts must pay the full high-tier fee on every action until each identity accumulates real history. A comet account that flares briefly then vanishes forfeits its accumulated discount, forcing re-payment. Honest agents hold a long-lived haven of low fees; attackers pay rising marginal cost per sybil as fees scale with fresh-identity count.
